key: An aunty back from a Char Dham yatra
name: ch07_aunty_yatra_wedding
alt: At a family wedding, a young professional leans in and listens while an older aunty happily tells her pilgrimage trek story, a mountain temple and a pony shown in her speech bubble.
scene: A wide view of an Indian wedding hall in the evening: marigold garlands strung across the top, a decorated stage with an empty swing far in the background, round tables with white cloths and steel tumblers. In the LEFT third, a young man in his late 20s (light blue kurta, neat haircut, small office lanyard tucked into his pocket) sits on a plastic chair leaning forward, elbows on knees, eyes bright, clearly listening. A small faded thought bubble above his head shows a tiny hotel bed and a suitcase, crossed out lightly, to show he set his own Europe trip aside. In the CENTRE-RIGHT, a cheerful aunty in her mid-60s (maroon silk sari, grey bun, spectacles, a sacred thread on her wrist) sits beside him gesturing with both hands, mid-story, beaming. A large speech bubble rises from her containing a snow-capped mountain, a zig-zag trail with a small pony and a pony man, and a stone temple at the top. On the far RIGHT, his mother (green sari) stands holding a plate of sweets and smiles proudly toward them. Warm golden light from hanging lamps, festive and gentle mood. Labels: "HER STORY" inside the top of the aunty's bubble, and "LISTENING" on the floor under the young man's chair.

key: At a Bengaluru house party you get stuck
name: ch07_rocket_engineer_party
alt: At a house party a young guest keeps asking "And then?" while a retired rocket engineer tells launch stories, a rocket rising in his speech bubble and a clock showing an hour passing.
scene: A cosy apartment living room during a house party at night, fairy lights along the window, a sofa, a small table with snacks, plates of samosas and a jug of juice. Other guests are blurred grey silhouettes chatting in the background on the right. In the LEFT foreground, a young woman (around 25, yellow kurti, jeans, holding a glass) sits sideways on the sofa arm, turned fully toward her neighbour, eyebrows raised, mouth open in a small question. A small speech bubble from her reads only "And then?" in short handwritten letters. In the CENTRE, a retired engineer in his early 70s (white hair, half-sleeve checked shirt, spectacles, a cardigan) sits in an armchair gesturing upward with one hand, eyes shining, deep in a story. A big speech bubble over him shows a plain white rocket with no markings lifting off from a launch tower in a cloud of smoke, with a small worried face beside a countdown screen. On the wall a round clock has a curved arrow sweeping a full hour around its face. On the far RIGHT, near the door, the host (middle-aged man, blue shirt) is shown later, shaking hands with the engineer, who points back at the young woman with a pleased smile. Warm yellow indoor light, friendly mood. Labels: "ASK" under the young woman, "HIS STORY" at the top of the big bubble.

name: ch07_family_doctor_listens
alt: Split picture: a small-town doctor turns her chair toward the patient with her pen down and listens; a big-hospital doctor types at a computer while the patient talks to his back.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same patient in both halves: a man in his 40s in a grey half-sleeve shirt, a hand on his chest, mid-cough, a small cough cloud near his mouth. LEFT panel: a small-town clinic with a wooden desk, a steel almirah, a calendar on a green wall and a ceiling fan. The doctor, a woman in her 50s with a white coat over a cotton sari, a stethoscope round her neck and reading glasses on her head, has turned her chair fully toward him, pen laid down on the prescription pad, nodding, one hand raised in a small question. The patient's speech bubble is long and wavy, showing a story. A green tick floats near the patient's relaxed shoulders. RIGHT panel: a bright modern hospital cubicle with a large monitor and a token-number screen. A younger doctor in a white coat faces the computer, typing fast, his back half-turned to the same patient, whose speech bubble shrinks and ends in a small grey question mark. The prescription printing from the printer is the same strip of tablets as on the left. Soft daylight on the left, cool blue light on the right. Labels: "HEARD" at the top of the left panel, "UNHEARD" at the top of the right panel.

key: You return a pressure cooker with a
name: ch07_cooker_shop_owner
alt: In a kitchenware shop the counter boy points at a no-returns board, while the owner at the cash desk turns a cracked cooker handle in his hands and listens to the customer.
scene: A street-facing kitchenware shop in an Indian city, steel vessels, pressure cookers and mixer boxes stacked on shelves up to the ceiling. On the LEFT, a teenage counter boy (red T-shirt, bored face) points over his shoulder with his thumb at a painted board on the wall that says "No Return" in short letters, while already turning to serve another customer holding a steel kadai. A red cross floats next to the board. In the CENTRE, a woman in her 30s (teal salwar kameez, cloth shopping bag on her arm) stands holding up a pressure cooker whose black handle shows a clear zig-zag crack. On the RIGHT, behind a raised wooden cash desk with a till and a small idol shelf, the owner (man in his 50s, white shirt, moustache, reading glasses pushed up) leans forward, waves her over with one hand and in the next moment is shown turning the cracked handle over in his hands, studying it, a small magnifier-like circle highlighting the crack. Above him a speech bubble holds a brand-new cooker box with a green tick. Dotted arrow from the woman to the owner shows her being called over. Warm afternoon light through the shutter, busy but friendly mood. Labels: "RULE" above the counter boy, "LISTEN" above the owner's desk.

key: Your father is reading the newspaper
name: ch07_father_folds_newspaper
alt: Split picture: a father talks to his child from behind a raised newspaper; then the same father folds the paper, puts it down and turns to the child, who glows.
scene: A split-panel breakfast scene divided by a thin vertical line, the same Indian dining table in both halves: steel plates with idli and chutney, a steel tumbler of filter coffee, a window with morning light. A small girl of about seven (school uniform, two plaited pigtails tied with ribbons) sits on a chair on the left of each panel, leaning toward her father and holding up a drawing of a house. LEFT panel: the father (man in his 40s, white vest under an open check shirt) holds a large open newspaper that hides his whole face; only his hands and the top of his hair show. A tiny speech line from behind the paper reads "hmm". The girl's shoulders drop and her drawing droops; a small grey cloud sits over her. RIGHT panel: the same father has folded the newspaper and laid it flat on the table beside his coffee, and turns his whole body to the girl, chin on his hand, smiling, looking at her drawing. The girl sits tall and beams, with little sparkle marks around her. The newspaper headline area is blank grey lines, unreadable, to show nobody remembers it. Warm yellow morning light. Labels: "BEHIND THE PAPER" at the top of the left panel, "PAPER DOWN" at the top of the right panel.

name: ch07_society_uncle_tea
alt: A housing-society secretary sits in a complaining uncle's flat drinking tea and listening, his pile of complaint letters on the table; later the uncle wears a committee badge and pays his dues.
scene: Inside a middle-class apartment living room in an Indian housing society: a sofa with a crochet cover, a wall clock, a framed photo of the building from long ago, a window showing parked cars below. In the CENTRE-LEFT, a retired uncle in his late 60s (white kurta pyjama, thick spectacles, grey moustache) sits in a cane chair, one finger raised mid-lecture, a thick stack of handwritten letters and printed emails piled on the teapot table beside him, the top sheet showing "1998" in short numbers. Facing him on the RIGHT, the new committee secretary, a woman in her late 30s (mustard cotton sari, a diary on her lap), holds a cup of tea, nodding, relaxed, eyes on him. Four empty teacups line up on the table, each a little behind the last, with a curved dotted arrow showing the passing weeks. In a round inset bubble at the top right, the same uncle is shown later, smiling, wearing a small badge on his kurta and handing a receipt over at the society office counter with a green tick. A small parked car icon with a parking P-sign appears faintly on his complaint pile. Calm late-afternoon light, gentle and slightly humorous mood. Labels: "COMPLAINTS" over the letter pile, "ON THE COMMITTEE" under the inset bubble.

name: ch07_kirana_khata_dispute
alt: An angry old customer shouts over a khata book at a kirana counter while the shopkeeper offers him a chair and water; in an inset a week later he returns with the money and a long list.
scene: A small neighbourhood kirana shop with wooden shelves of rice sacks, dal jars, biscuit packets, a steel weighing scale and a hanging bunch of bananas. On the LEFT, an old customer in his early 70s (white shirt, dhoti, walking stick, white hair) leans over the counter, red-faced, one finger stabbing at an open ruled khata notebook, his mouth wide in a shout, little jagged anger lines around his head and a speech bubble holding only "600". Behind the counter on the RIGHT, the shopkeeper (man in his 40s, cream kurta, sandalwood mark on forehead) is calm, hands open, offering a plastic chair with one hand and a steel glass of water with the other; a soft speech bubble from him shows a pen striking out a line in the notebook. Between them a dashed arrow shows the angry lines softening into a small smile. In a rounded inset at the top right labelled with a small "next week" tag, the same uncle comes back, a little sheepish, holding out folded notes in one hand and a long paper shopping list in the other, while the shopkeeper grins. Warm morning light, homely mood. Labels: "LET HIM FINISH" above the shopkeeper, "BACK AGAIN" under the inset.

name: ch07_student_email_founder
alt: A first-year student in a hostel room writes a short, thoughtful question to a busy founder, whose inbox is full of identical referral requests, and the founder answers that one.
scene: A split view joined by a long dashed arrow. LEFT: a small engineering-college hostel room at night, a steel bunk bed, a bucket, a bare table lamp. A first-year student (about 18, thin, plain T-shirt, rubber slippers) sits on the bed with a laptop, a printed magazine interview open beside him with lines underlined in pen. On his laptop screen a short email with three tidy lines and a small question mark. From the laptop a dashed arrow travels across the top of the picture to the RIGHT side. RIGHT: a modern glass office corner at dusk; a founder in his 40s (navy polo shirt, short beard, generic plain laptop) sits at a desk. Behind him a tall tower of identical grey envelope icons stacks up, all the same, with tiny grey blank lines, to show a hundred requests that look alike. One envelope, coloured amber with a question mark, sits apart on his desk, and he is reading it, leaning in with a hand on his chin, smiling. His reply flows back as a long multi-line letter along a second dashed arrow toward the student, ending in a small calendar card with a meetup date. Cool evening light on the right, lamp-yellow on the left, hopeful mood. Labels: "REFER ME" across the grey envelope pile, "REAL QUESTION" over the amber envelope.

key: Your friend calls at 11 p.m. from Pune
name: ch07_late_call_just_listen
alt: Split picture of a late-night phone call: first the listener fires off advice and the upset friend goes quiet; next time he just listens and she ends calm, with her own plan.
scene: A split-panel night scene divided by a thin vertical line, each panel itself split in two by a phone-call zig-zag. In each panel, a young woman (late 20s, loose T-shirt, hair in a messy bun) sits on her bed in a small rented flat with a city skyline at the window and a wall clock showing eleven; and a young man (late 20s, grey hoodie) sits at a desk in his own room, phone to his ear. LEFT panel: the man talks fast, counting points on his fingers, a speech bubble crammed with checklist icons, an envelope and a file folder pouring toward her. The woman has gone silent, looking away, a tiny grey ellipsis bubble over her head and her knees hugged up. RIGHT panel: the same man leans back with his eyes soft, phone to ear, a small bubble that holds only a heart-shaped sigh, while a large wavy speech bubble flows from the woman, full of squiggly lines, a small office desk and a frowning boss icon. At the bottom of her panel she stands up with a light bulb above her and a tiny note card with a tick, her own plan. Cool blue night light, soft warm lamp glow in the right panel. Labels: "ADVICE" at the top of the left panel, "JUST LISTEN" at the top of the right panel.

key: A good Carnatic music guru listening
name: ch07_music_guru_listens
alt: A Carnatic music teacher sits with eyes half-closed keeping the beat on her knee while a student sings on a mat; a stumbling note is met with a gentle nod.
scene: A calm music room in an old South Indian house: red oxide floor, a wooden pillar, a framed picture of a veena on the wall, morning light from a barred window. On a woven mat in the CENTRE-RIGHT, the guru, a woman in her 60s (cream silk sari with a maroon border, grey hair in a bun, small bindi, jasmine in her hair), sits cross-legged, eyes half-closed in deep attention, one palm tapping the beat on her knee with small curved motion lines, head tilted slightly, a faint smile, no frown. Beside her a tanpura stands upright with soft wavy lines rising from its strings. On the LEFT, facing her on the mat, a girl of about 14 (green pavadai, long plait) sings with one hand raised, a line of musical notes flowing from her mouth toward the guru; one note in the middle of the line is wobbly and slips off the line. Where it wobbles, the guru's small nod is shown with two tiny curved nod marks and no cross. A soft warm glow joins the notes to the guru's ear, showing every note is heard. The student's face is eager, not afraid. Golden morning light, peaceful mood. Labels: "EVERY NOTE HEARD" at the top centre, "TALA" next to the guru's tapping hand.

key: The relative at every family function
name: ch07_relative_turns_to_himself
alt: At a family function a relative turns every topic to himself, his speech bubbles full of his own trophies and wedding, and the group he walks toward quietly breaks apart.
scene: A family function in a decorated hall courtyard, marigold strings above, plastic chairs, a buffet table with steel chafing dishes in the background. In the CENTRE, a portly relative in his late 50s (shiny silk kurta, gold watch, thick moustache) talks loudly, thumb pointing at his own chest. A young man on the LEFT (blue shirt, holding a new office ID card) has a small speech bubble with a briefcase icon; the relative's much bigger bubble swallows it, showing a trophy and the number "1995". Next to him a young woman cousin (pink lehenga) holds a small bubble with two rings, and again his large bubble overwrites it with a bag of money and a big wedding stage. Both young people smile politely with stiff faces, small sweat drops at their temples. On the RIGHT, the relative steps toward a group of four guests standing in a circle; as he approaches, the guests drift away in different directions with small motion arrows, one checking a phone, one heading to the buffet, one waving to someone far away, leaving an empty circle on the floor where they stood. Bright festive daylight, wry humorous mood. Labels: "ME, ME, ME" above the relative, "EMPTY CIRCLE" on the floor at the right.

key: A chai-stall owner near a Bengaluru
name: ch07_chai_stall_remembers
alt: A chai-stall owner near a tech park hands out glasses of tea and asks each regular about their own news: a baby, a visa, an onsite trip.
scene: A roadside chai stall at morning outside a glass office park, a tin roof, a big aluminium kettle on a gas stove, glass jars of biscuits and rusk, a bench in front. Behind the stall, the chai-wallah (man in his 40s, checked lungi, sleeveless sweater over a shirt, towel on his shoulder) pours tea from a height into small glasses, his mouth open in a question, his face warm and curious. In front, three office regulars stand with glasses: on the LEFT a young man in a blue shirt with an ID lanyard; in the CENTRE a woman in a kurta and jeans with a laptop bag; on the RIGHT an older man with spectacles and a backpack. Above each regular floats a small thought icon the chai-wallah remembers: a baby's rattle over the young man, a passport with a stamp over the woman, a small aeroplane over the older man. Thin dotted lines link each icon to a matching small icon in a neat thought bubble above the chai-wallah's head, like a memory board. The chai-wallah's own speech is tiny, and the customers' speech bubbles are big and happy. A calendar on the stall post has many days ticked to show years of regulars. Fresh morning light, busy traffic faintly behind. Labels: "HE REMEMBERS" above the chai-wallah, "REGULARS" under the bench.
